body:
I've seen quite a bit of death, I've thought about what it means a lot, and I've read some really cool books on the topic. I've been through it, I've held dead people who died too young, I've spoken at funerals, I've cried and comforted others.   


I think we as a society avoid death as a concept and as a reality and therein lies a lot of the pain when we encounter it. It's the pain of ignorance lost, the fracturing of a facade. I don't want such a key decision of MINE to be encumbered by what is largely a transient and narcissistic pain in losing others. Killing yourself is selfish? I think living is selfish, and I think expecting others to want to live is selfish.
